ESP32-WROOM-32, seen from above, the antenna at the top, 3V3\'s side on the left. The GPIOs work at 3.3 V. ADC2 can\'t be read while Wi-Fi is on.
ESP32-WROOM-32, 30 pins, seen from above, the antenna at the top, EN\'s side on the left. The GPIOs work at 3.3 V. ADC2 can\'t be read while Wi-Fi is on; the LED is on GPIO2.
AI-Thinker\'s board, 5V\'s side on the left, 5V and 3V3 at the top. No USB on it: it\'s programmed through U0R and U0T, IO0 held to GND. The microSD card takes GPIO2, 4 and 12–15.
ESP32-S3-WROOM-1, seen from above, the antenna at the top, 3V3\'s side on the left. GPIO19 and 20 are the chip\'s own USB. ADC2 can\'t be read while Wi-Fi is on.
Seen from above, USB at the top, 5V\'s side on the left. The GPIOs work at 3.3 V; the BOOT button is on GPIO9. Some clones have their pins in another order: check the board\'s printing.
ESP8266 (ESP-12), seen from above, the antenna at the top, A0\'s side on the left. The D numbers are printed on the board, the GPIOs\' are what the code uses; they work at 3.3 V.
ESP8266, seen from above, the antenna at the top, RST\'s side on the left. The D numbers as on the NodeMCU; the GPIOs work at 3.3 V.
